title: Enterprise AI Operating Model Review
summary: The team aligned on a narrow initial operating model and agreed to keep the executive report concise. The primary constraint is not data volume but uneven content density across sections.

insights.title: Governance is the dominant constraint
insights.description: The organization has enough technical capability to launch the first use cases, but ownership, approval boundaries, exception handling, auditability, and escalation rules remain fragmented across several functions. Without a single operating model, teams are likely to create duplicate controls and slow down execution even when the underlying AI capability is ready. The recommended next step is to define one accountable owner, one approved policy layer, and a small number of measurable control points before expanding the use-case portfolio.

insights.title: Adoption should be measured by completed work
insights.description: Usage counts alone will not prove operational value.

insights.title: Keep the first portfolio narrow
insights.description: A small number of high-frequency workflows will produce cleaner evidence than a broad catalogue.

decisions.title: Create one governance layer
decisions.description: Centralize policy, audit and escalation rules.

decisions.title: Launch with six teams
decisions.description: Use the first cohort as a controlled operational benchmark.

risks.title: Control fragmentation
risks.description: Parallel approval models may recreate manual bottlenecks.

tasks.task: Define the accountable owner and approval boundaries for the pilot
Publish baseline metrics and the first operational scorecard
